Hi Avery — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

What we covered
- Walked through the payment-notification demo and where you saw latency spikes (peak 450ms p95 on your demo traffic).
- Discussed data residency (US-only), and need for deterministic output on payment-extraction fields.
- Procurement/SC details: Samir will own the PO & SOC2 path.

Attachments I’m sending with this note
- finovate_prompt_set_v1.csv (30 canonical prompts + negative cases used in the demo)
- latency_cost_estimates_256t.xlsx (initial back-of-envelope for three model options)

Shortlist we recommend for the 2-week POC (high-level rationale):
1) RW-4-7B-q4 — best cost/latency balance for extraction tasks; quantized, low token cost.
2) Llama2-13B-8bit — stronger on long-context synthesis with slightly higher latency/cost; good for edge-case recovery.
3) Mistral-Instruct-7B — very high throughput in our hosted tests, lower hallucination on template fills.

Why these three: they span the tradeoffs you asked about — cost per 1k tokens, p95 latency at 256 tokens, and measured quality on our 30-prompt eval. I’ve included the mini-eval report for the same prompts (see attachment).

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP)
- Week 0 (this week): sign SOW / PO (Samir) and finalize model choice for POC (you + us).
- Week 1: deploy two candidates to a dedicated test pool under your VPC (we’ll do RW-4-7B-q4 + one larger model).
- Week 2: run prompt set + live traffic shadowing; evaluate accuracy, latency, and cost delta.

Success criteria suggestion (we can refine)
- Extraction accuracy >= 92% F1 on canonical fields
- p95 latency <= 250ms for 95% of traffic
- Cost delta vs baseline <= 1.8x

Next asks for you
- Confirm PO contact (Samir) and target kickoff week
- Any additional prompt examples you want included in the eval

If that sounds good I’ll loop in Solutions for the deployment kickoff.

Hi Avery — quick one-pager in-line below plus attached mini-eval with the 30 prompts (results summary).

Shortlist + one-line tradeoffs (for 5M tokens/month, typical request ~120 tokens):
- RW-4-7B-q4
  • Cost est: ~$0.12 / 1K tokens (quantized path) — ~ $600/month
  • p95 latency (256t): ~180–220 ms (single-GPU continuous batching)
  • Quality (eval avg): 0.87 accept rate; hallucination ~3.5%
  • Notes: Best baseline for extraction; lowest operational cost; supports our KV-cache for templates.

- Llama2-13B-8bit
  • Cost est: ~$0.38 / 1K tokens — ~ $1,900/month
  • p95 latency (256t): ~350–420 ms
  • Quality (eval avg): 0.92 accept rate; hallucination ~2.1%
  • Notes: Higher quality on ambiguous contexts but heavier resource needs.

- Mistral-Instruct-7B
  • Cost est: ~$0.20 / 1K tokens — ~ $1,000/month
  • p95 latency (256t): ~230–300 ms
  • Quality (eval avg): 0.89 accept rate; hallucination ~2.8%
  • Notes: Very good throughput on our multi-request experiments; competitive quality for templated outputs.

Regression monitoring + rollback
- We sandbox candidate models behind a traffic-splitting policy (canary at 1%) and run the full prompt set + a holdout of live traffic.
- We compute key signals every 10 minutes: extraction F1 on golden set, hallucination rate, and token-efficiency.
- If any signal breaches threshold (e.g., >5% drop in F1 or >2x hallucination relative to baseline) an automatic rollback policy re-routes to the pinned model and alerts SRE/CS.
- We’ll provide a snapshot comparison report (diff of outputs) and an automated regression alert to your Slack/procurement inbox during the POC.

Attachments: mini-eval-report-20270720.pdf (30-prompt results, example failure cases), latency_cost_estimates_256t.xlsx (detailed line items).

Recommendation for the POC: start with RW-4-7B-q4 + Llama2-13B-8bit as the second comparator. That combination lets you validate extraction at low cost while ensuring coverage for ambiguous cases.

I’ll drop the short one-pager PDF by EOD.
